invariant_families.name: Authoritative production records
invariant_families.applies_when: The product owns authoritative production business records.

invariant_families.name: Material offline continuity
invariant_families.applies_when: People must continue material work while network connectivity is unavailable.

invariant_families.name: Multi-organization isolation
invariant_families.applies_when: The product stores or processes data for more than one organization or tenant.

invariant_families.name: Real payment processing
invariant_families.applies_when: The product initiates or controls real funds movement or receives authoritative payment callbacks.

invariant_families.name: Sensitive data protection
invariant_families.applies_when: The product stores or processes sensitive personal or business data.

invariants.name: Authoritative record ownership
invariants.description: The route provides a durable authoritative data boundary rather than presentation-only fixtures.

invariants.name: Durable local operations
invariants.description: Material offline work is captured durably on the local device before synchronization.

invariants.name: Explicit synchronization protocol
invariants.description: Local operations synchronize through an explicit, versioned protocol.

invariants.name: Conflict handling
invariants.description: Concurrent offline and server changes have defined conflict-detection and resolution behavior.

invariants.name: Idempotent server application
invariants.description: Replayed synchronized operations can be applied safely without duplicating effects.

invariants.name: Organization data-owner boundary
invariants.description: Every organization-owned record carries an explicit and authoritative owner or tenant boundary.

invariants.name: Server-side organization isolation
invariants.description: Organization isolation is enforced on the server and cannot rely only on client-side filtering.

invariants.name: Payment callback authenticity
invariants.description: Authoritative payment callbacks or provider messages are authenticated before processing.

invariants.name: Idempotent payment processing
invariants.description: Repeated payment commands and callbacks cannot duplicate a financial effect.

invariants.name: Payment reconciliation
invariants.description: Internal payment state is reconciled against the authoritative provider record.

invariants.name: Payment failure recovery
invariants.description: Timeouts, retries, partial failures, refunds, and recovery paths have explicit state handling.

invariants.name: Server-side authorization
invariants.description: Access to sensitive data is authorized at the trusted server boundary.

invariants.name: Sensitive-data auditability
invariants.description: Material access and changes to sensitive data produce an auditable record.

invariants.name: Retention and deletion handling
invariants.description: Sensitive-data retention and deletion behavior is explicit and enforceable.

invariants.name: Storage and transit protection
invariants.description: Sensitive data is protected while stored and while transmitted.

patterns.name: Static demonstration
patterns.fit: A disposable or presentation-only experience with no authoritative production state.
patterns.shape: Static client assets with fixtures or a narrowly scoped hosted endpoint.
hard_limits: Not suitable for authoritative business records, real payments, or multi-user workflow state.

patterns.name: Managed modular monolith
patterns.fit: The default for an MVP or early production web product whose team values delivery speed and low operational load.
patterns.shape: One cohesive application deployment, explicit domain modules, a managed relational database, and managed identity and storage.
hard_limits: Continuous connectivity is assumed unless a separate offline capability is designed.
Module boundaries must remain explicit even though deployment is shared.

patterns.name: Separated API, monolithic service
patterns.fit: Multiple first-party clients need one stable application API, while a distributed backend would add unjustified complexity.
patterns.shape: Web or mobile clients call one versioned API backed by a modular monolithic service and one primary data boundary.
hard_limits: An API boundary adds compatibility and deployment coordination costs.
It is not a reason to split domain services prematurely.

patterns.name: Self-hosted modular monolith
patterns.fit: A real deployment-control, locality, or vendor constraint justifies owning infrastructure operations.
patterns.shape: A modular application and relational database deployed on controlled infrastructure with explicit backup, restore, patching, and monitoring ownership.
hard_limits: The team accepts ongoing security patching, availability, backup, and incident-response duties.

patterns.name: Offline-first specialized route
patterns.fit: People must continue material work through network outages and later reconcile authoritative state.
patterns.shape: A durable local operation store, explicit synchronization protocol, conflict rules, idempotent server application, and visible sync status.
hard_limits: Synchronization semantics, conflict resolution, migration compatibility, and recovery materially increase delivery and testing scope.
Security and data-retention rules must also cover local copies.
